div.p: url: Ordering straight from the unit
version: 1.0.0
name: DirectOrderScenario
title: Ordering straight from the unit
status: Active
experimental: true
publisher: José Costa Teixeira
contact: José Costa Teixeira: https://github.com/costateixeira, José Costa Teixeira: you-know.it@gmail.com
description:
A placer posts an order to a Spenser unit and gets back the dispense. No server, no Task, no tag: the POST is the authorization.
jurisdiction: World
purpose:

The short way round. There is no order server here, so nothing has to make the order actionable: posting it at the unit is itself the instruction to dispense, and the servo has already turned by the time the unit answers.
This is the route to start from when trying a unit out, and the one a workshop runs on when the network is somebody's phone.
Whatever is asking for chocolate: a script, a client under development, or the unit's own dashboard.
One dispenser, acting here only as a FHIR server.
A MedicationRequest naming a chocolate from the IG's own code system. Neither the actionable tag nor a Task is needed on this route.

blockquote.p: content: MedicationRequest: status = active; intent = instance-order

div.p: What the unit returns, pointing back at the order in authorizingPrescription. An absent whenHandedOver means the unit's clock has not been set by NTP, not that the time is unknown.

blockquote.p: title: Order a chocolate from the unit

div.p: One request, one chocolate.
The unit is on the network and the placer can reach it. The lane for the code being ordered has stock.
A chocolate has been dispensed, and the unit holds a MedicationDispense recording it.

The unit dispenses before it answers. The response is 201 Created carrying the MedicationDispense, with a Location for the record the unit kept and an ETag. This changes the unit, so it needs the unit's key.
Nothing moves, and the unit still answers with a MedicationDispense: status of declined, and notPerformedReason.concept of outofstock. A refusal is an answer, not an error.

blockquote.p: title: The order asks for something the unit does not carry

div.p: The unit answers 400 with an OperationOutcome. Every error from a FHIR route on the unit is an OperationOutcome; there is no second error format.

Optional, and open: reads need no key. The unit keeps what it dispensed, so the record can be read back later. The searchset also carries an entry with search.mode of outcome, saying when the unit last looked for work and how that went.
